title: Zoning for a glass studio: districts, home occupations, special use permits, site plans and the Zoning Clearance
question: Where in Albemarle County can I run a hot glass studio with classes and sales, what zoning approvals do I need (Zoning Clearance, special use permit, site plan, home occupation), and what do they cost?
office: Community Development Department: Zoning Division (Zoning Administrator; zoning clearances, determinations, home occupations, sign permits) and Planning Division (pre-application meetings, special use permits, site plans, Architectural Review Board); the Planning Commission and Board of Supervisors decide special use permits and special exceptions; the Board of Zoning Appeals hears appeals
summary: Albemarle's Zoning Ordinance is County Code Chapter 18 (on Municode; it is cited here, not copied). The first question is the parcel's district. Industrial districts in the Development Areas (Light Industry and Heavy Industry) allow manufacturing and fabrication by right; commercial districts allow retail sales and instruction, and whether furnace work fits is a classification call for the Zoning Administrator (a written Letter of Determination costs $220 plus 4% and can take 90 days); the Rural Areas allow a home occupation inside the home or, for a Major Home Occupation, an accessory building, within limits on floor area, customers, employees and sales, with anything bigger needing a special use permit. Every new commercial or industrial business then needs a Zoning Clearance ($60 plus 4%) filed in Civic Access before the tenant up-fit building permit and before any sign permit; a new building or changed site layout needs a site development plan ($1,775 plus 4% for an initial site plan) and, in an Entrance Corridor, a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Architectural Review Board or staff. A use listed only by special use permit goes through a mandatory pre-application meeting, a $2,365 plus 4% application with a $235 notice fee, and public hearings before the Planning Commission and Board of Supervisors. Zoning decisions can be appealed to the Board of Zoning Appeals within 30 days.

legal_basis.quote: For the granting of special exceptions under suitable regulations and safeguards; notwithstanding any other provisions of this article, the governing body of any locality may reserve unto itself the right to issue such special exceptions.
The zoning administrator shall have all necessary authority on behalf of the governing body to administer and enforce the zoning ordinance.
Any such violation shall be a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not more than $1,000.

For the collection of fees to cover the cost of making inspections, issuing permits, advertising of notices and other expenses incident to the administration of a zoning ordinance or to the filing or processing of any appeal or amendment thereto.
For the submission and approval of a plan of development prior to the issuance of building permits to assure compliance with regulations contained in such zoning ordinance.

This schedule of civil penalties shall be uniform for each type of specified violation, and the penalty for any one violation shall be a civil penalty of not more than $200 for the initial summons and not more than $500 for each additional summons.
The appeal shall be taken within 30 days after the decision appealed from by filing with the zoning administrator, and with the board, a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof.

steps.step: Find the parcel's zoning district, Development Area or Rural Area status, and overlays
steps.who: You; Community Development zoning staff if you cannot tell
steps.how: Open the County GIS-Web viewer (linked from the Home Occupations page as 'County GIS') and read the parcel's zoning district, whether it is inside a Development Area or in the Rural Areas, and whether an Entrance Corridor (EC) overlay, floodplain, steep slopes or stream buffers apply. The zoning district decides whether a hot shop is a by-right use, a special use, a home occupation, or not allowed; the Entrance Corridor decides whether the Architectural Review Board must approve the building, signs and outdoor equipment such as gas tanks and exhaust stacks. You can also ask Community Development's Property Inquiry service.
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Home Occupations page (County GIS link); County Code page (Property Inquiry)
steps.paraphrase: The rules depend on the zoning district and the kind of business; the County GIS shows the district.

steps.step: Match the studio's activities to the district's use list, and get a Letter of Determination if the fit is unclear
steps.who: You; the Zoning Administrator (Community Development Zoning Division)
steps.how: Read the district's section of the Zoning Ordinance (County Code Chapter 18 on Municode): the Light Industry (LI) and Heavy Industry (HI) districts list manufacturing, processing, assembly and fabrication uses by right; the commercial districts (C-1 Commercial, CO Commercial Office, HC Highway Commercial, PD-SC and the Downtown Crozet district among others) list retail sales, services and instruction; the Rural Areas (RA) district lists farm and home-based uses with most commercial uses only by special use permit. A hot shop (gas furnace, glory hole, kilns) is production; a gallery with classes is retail and instruction; a demonstration space where more than 50 people gather is also an assembly use for building and fire purposes. If you cannot tell which use name applies, or whether accessory production is allowed with a retail use, file an Official Letter of Determination application in Civic Access ($220 plus 4%); the letter is the County's formal, appealable answer and can take up to 90 days.
steps.deadline: Letter of Determination: up to 90 days to issue
steps.fee: Official Letter of Determination: $220, plus the 4% technology surcharge
steps.basis: Albemarle County Code Chapter 18 (Zoning Ordinance) district regulations (Municode, not reprinted); Determinations and Appeals page; Community Development fee schedule
steps.paraphrase: On a formal request, the Zoning Administrator writes a Letter of Determination on how a use is classified or how the zoning rules apply to it.

steps.step: If you want to work from home: check the home occupation limits, and whether you need a clearance or a special use permit
steps.how: A home occupation must be run by an occupant of the home, must not interfere with the neighborhood, and needs an approved Home Occupation Clearance before it starts ($30 plus 4%). In the Rural Areas there are two clearances: Minor (inside the dwelling only) and Major (may use an accessory structure with the same setbacks as the house). Both are limited to 25% of the dwelling's gross floor area or 1,500 square feet, whichever is less; customers up to 10 vehicle trips a day or 30 a week, six days a week, 7 am to 8 pm; sales only of items crafted on site or directly related to the occupation; up to two non-resident employees; one sign; on-site parking; materials stored inside. The County page's list of prohibited rural home occupations starts with any use that would need a special use permit and includes restaurants, so a cafe cannot ride along with a home studio. In residential districts (R-1 through R-15, PUD, PRD, NMD) a Class A clearance covers an in-home occupation with no employees and up to seven customer visits a week; a Class B occupation (employees, or an accessory building) needs a special use permit ($1,185 plus 4%). Rules marked with an asterisk on the County page can be waived by special exception ($980 plus 4%). A furnace-scale hot shop will usually exceed what a home occupation allows; ask at the pre-application meeting.
steps.deadline: Clearance approved before the business starts
steps.fee: Home Occupation Clearance: $30, plus 4%; Special Use Permit, home occupation Class B: $1,185, plus 4%; Special Exception: $980, plus 4%
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Home Occupations page (Internet Archive copy of 12 June 2026) and Learn More About Home Occupations page (Internet Archive copy of 15 May 2026); Community Development fee schedule; Zoning Ordinance § 5.2 (Municode)
steps.paraphrase: Get the Home Occupation Clearance approved before you start the business.

steps.step: Hold the pre-application meeting (mandatory before a special use permit or rezoning; exploratory for everything else)
steps.who: You; Community Development Planning, Zoning and Engineering staff (cdd-preapps@albemarle.org)
steps.how: Email or call the pre-application coordinator, file the Pre-Application Meeting Request in Civic Access (Request, then Pre-Application Meeting), and send a conceptual sketch plan showing the parcel, entrance, building or area to be used, parking, and environmental features by 12 noon on a Monday. Meetings are Mondays at 2, 3 or 4 pm on Microsoft Teams and are free. For a special use permit the meeting is mandatory and cannot take place until at least two weeks before an official submittal deadline on the SP/ZMA schedule; at an exploratory meeting staff will say whether a mandatory one is still needed or is waived by the Director of Planning. Staff also tell you what supplemental information the application must contain.
steps.deadline: Request and sketch plan by 12 pm Monday; mandatory meeting scheduled within two weeks
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Pre-Application Meeting page (Internet Archive copy of 14 August 2026); Zoning Ordinance §§ 33.14, 33.31 (Municode)
steps.paraphrase: A mandatory pre-application meeting cannot take place more than two weeks before the official submittal deadline it precedes.

steps.step: If the district lists the use only by special use permit: apply for the special use permit
steps.who: You or your agent; Planning Division staff; the Planning Commission (recommendation) and Board of Supervisors (decision)
steps.how: Submit the Special Use Permit application in Civic Access on a date in the County's SP/ZMA submittal and review schedule, with the checklist items and the supplemental information named at the pre-application meeting. The fee for most special use permits is $2,365 plus 4%, which covers the application and the first resubmittal, plus the required-notice base fee of $235 plus the actual postage and advertising cost; later resubmittals and applicant-requested deferrals of a scheduled public hearing carry their own fees. Staff review the project against the Comprehensive Plan and any Master Plan, a community meeting may be required, and the Planning Commission and Board of Supervisors hold public hearings; the Board may attach conditions. Sign-related special use permits (off-site and electric message signs) go to the Board of Zoning Appeals instead.
steps.deadline: Per the SP/ZMA submittal and review schedule
steps.fee: Special Use Permit, all other: $2,365 plus 4%, plus the $235 notice base fee and actual postage and advertising; deferral of a scheduled public hearing at the applicant's request: the actual cost of postage and advertisement
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Special Use Permits page (Internet Archive copy of 8 May 2026); Community Development fee schedule; Va. Code § 15.2-2286(A)(3); Zoning Ordinance § 33 (Municode)
steps.paraphrase: A special use can be refused at a particular spot because of its intensity, disturbance or appearance, or because it conflicts with the County's adopted plans.

steps.step: If a specific zoning rule stands in the way and the ordinance allows it to be waived: apply for a special exception
steps.who: You; Planning staff; Board of Supervisors
steps.how: A special exception can waive, modify or vary a Zoning Ordinance requirement only where that section says it may be waived or modified by special exception (for example some home occupation limits, setbacks or site plan drawing requirements). It is filed in Civic Access as 'Special Exception – Site Plans, Zoning Map Amendments, Special Use Permits, Home Occupations, Homestays, all other Zoning Special Exceptions', is reviewed together with the related site plan or special use permit, and is decided by the Board of Supervisors under Zoning Ordinance § 33.9. The fee is $980 plus 4%.
steps.deadline: Filed with, and reviewed alongside, the related application
steps.fee: Special Exception: $980, plus the 4% technology surcharge
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Special Exceptions, Variations & Waivers page (Internet Archive copy of 14 April 2026); Community Development fee schedule; Zoning Ordinance §§ 3.1, 33.9 (Municode)
steps.paraphrase: Special exceptions are reviewed at the same time as the site plan, special use permit or rezoning they go with.

steps.step: For a new building, addition or changed site layout: get the site development plan approved (and Entrance Corridor approval)
steps.who: Your engineer or surveyor; Planning Division; the Site Review Committee; the Architectural Review Board or its staff in an Entrance Corridor
steps.how: Developing land for a commercial or industrial use needs a site plan. Review the Initial Site Plan Checklist, then file the Initial Site Plan in Civic Access ($1,775 plus 4%); the Site Review Committee (County departments, VDOT, ACSA, Fire Rescue and the Health Department as needed) reviews it, after which the Final Site Plan is reviewed administratively. Changes to an already approved site plan use a Minor Site Plan Amendment ($590 plus 4%) or a Letter of Revision ($120 plus 4%); a Major Amendment is $1,775 plus 4%. In an Entrance Corridor the building, site lighting and rooftop or ground-mounted equipment need a Certificate of Appropriateness; nine categories (for example equipment, lighting, minor amendments, and building permits changing half or less of an elevation) can be approved by staff as county-wide Certificates of Appropriateness without an ARB meeting (staff review of a county-wide certificate $265 to $540 plus 4%; ARB board review of a site plan $1,185 plus 4%). The commercial building permit cannot be issued without the approved site plan number and date.
steps.fee: Initial Site Plan, Final Site Plan or Major Amendment: $1,775 plus 4%; Preapplication Plan and Minor Amendment: $590 plus 4%; Letter of Revision: $120 plus 4%; ARB major board review (site plan): $1,185 plus 4%
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Site Development Plans page (Internet Archive copy of 12 April 2026), Entrance Corridors page (Internet Archive copy of 5 March 2026), Commercial Building Permits page; Community Development fee schedule; Va. Code § 15.2-2286(A)(8); Zoning Ordinance § 32 (Municode)
steps.paraphrase: The Site Review Committee reviews initial site plans and major amendments.

steps.step: Apply for the Zoning Clearance for a business in a commercial or industrial space
steps.who: You (the business or tenant), or a representative such as your contractor; Community Development Zoning Division
steps.how: In Civic Access choose Zoning Clearance, then 'Business in a Commercial or Industrial Space'. The clearance belongs to the business and must be filled out and signed by the business representative even when someone else submits it. It confirms the use is allowed at the address and records parking and other limits, and it may depend on other approvals: Architectural Review Board approval, acceptance of a Certified Engineer's Report (the County's form for industrial uses with emissions, noise or other performance standards, which a gas-fired hot shop should expect to need), Health Department approval, or VDOT approval. The fee is $60 plus 4%. A new tenant's Zoning Clearance must be approved before the tenant up-fit building permit is issued, and before any sign permit; a change of name, ownership or location needs a new clearance.
steps.deadline: Approved before the building permit for interior alterations and before any sign permit
steps.fee: Zoning Clearance, all other uses: $60, plus the 4% technology surcharge
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Zoning Clearance page (Internet Archive copy of 16 March 2026), Commercial Building Permits page (Internet Archive copy of 16 March 2026), Sign Permits page (Internet Archive copy of 17 April 2026); Community Development fee schedule
steps.paraphrase: The clearance can depend on other sign-offs: the Architectural Review Board, a Certified Engineer's Report, the Health Department or VDOT.

steps.step: Pass the zoning inspections that go with the building permit and certificate of occupancy
steps.who: Zoning staff; you or your contractor request them in Civic Access
steps.how: Zoning reviews the building permit for use, setbacks and site-plan conformity, and a preliminary and a final zoning inspection ($25 each) are part of the building permit path; the final zoning inspection must pass before the certificate of occupancy. Inspections are requested in the Civic Access portal. Keep the approved site plan and clearance conditions (parking, screening, hours, outdoor storage) in mind when placing gas tanks, exhaust stacks and cullet storage outdoors.
steps.deadline: Final zoning inspection before the certificate of occupancy
steps.fee: Zoning inspection: $25 each (preliminary or final), plus 4%
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Commercial Building Permits page (Internet Archive copy of 16 March 2026); Community Development fee schedule
steps.paraphrase: Inspection requests go through the Civic Access portal, which needs a registered account.

steps.step: Get the sign permit after the clearance
steps.who: You or your sign contractor; Zoning Division; ARB staff in an Entrance Corridor
steps.how: Permanent and temporary signs each need a sign permit under Zoning Ordinance § 4.15 (window signs up to 25% of the window, home occupation signs and some others are exempt but still limited in size and setback). File the Sign Permit Application in Civic Access with sign drawings and a plat for a monument a sign permit usually takes about 10 business days, not counting Architectural Review Board review. In an Entrance Corridor the sign needs a Certificate of Appropriateness, usually approved by staff when it meets the ARB Sign Guidelines and any Comprehensive Sign Plan for a multi-tenant building. Temporary sign permits last 15 days each, up to six a year and 60 days total. An electric sign also needs an electrical trade permit.
steps.deadline: After the Zoning Clearance; sign permits typically processed within 10 business days
steps.fee: Sign permit, ARB not required (temporary signs): $30 plus 4%; sign permit, ARB required: $140 plus 4%; Entrance Corridor review of a sign: $130 plus 4% (resubmittal $65); Electric - Signs trade permit: $55
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Sign Permits page (Internet Archive copy of 17 April 2026); Community Development fee schedule; Zoning Ordinance § 4.15 (Municode)
steps.paraphrase: Sign permits usually take about 10 business days, not counting any ARB approval.

steps.step: If a lender or landlord asks: order a Letter of Zoning Compliance
steps.how: A Letter of Zoning Compliance lists the property's current improvements, zoning, uses and any potential violations; lenders often ask for one. File it in Civic Access; it may take up to 30 days, it is not an interpretation and cannot be appealed, and it carries a fee (not listed on the pages read).
steps.fee: A fee applies (amount not shown on the page read; ask Community Development)
steps.basis: Albemarle County Community Development, Zoning Compliance page (Internet Archive copy of 17 March 2026)
steps.paraphrase: A Letter of Zoning Compliance can take up to 30 days.

escalation.trigger: The Zoning Administrator's determination, a refused Zoning Clearance, or another zoning decision you disagree with
escalation.next: Appeal to the Board of Zoning Appeals: file the Appeal of Zoning Administrator's Determination in Civic Access (notice of appeal filed with the zoning administrator and the board), fee $350 plus 4%
escalation.deadline: Within 30 days of the notice of the decision; 10 days for decisions on temporary or seasonal commercial uses; otherwise the determination becomes final and unappealable
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 15.2-2311(A); Albemarle County Determinations and Appeals page (Internet Archive copy of 12 May 2026); Community Development fee schedule
escalation.paraphrase: A determination can be appealed within 30 days of the notice under Va. Code § 15.2-2311, but decisions on temporary or seasonal commercial uses must be appealed within 10 days.

escalation.trigger: The Board of Supervisors denies the special use permit or special exception
escalation.next: Reapply with changes (a resubmittal or reapplication of a withdrawn application carries a fee), or seek judicial review of the Board's decision in circuit court
escalation.deadline: Judicial review of a governing body's zoning decision is generally sought within 30 days of the decision (Va. Code § 15.2-2285(F)); confirm with counsel
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 15.2-2285; Community Development fee schedule
escalation.quote: Every action contesting a decision of the local governing body adopting or failing to adopt a proposed zoning ordinance or amendment thereto or granting or failing to grant a special exception shall be filed within 30 days of the decision with the circuit court having jurisdiction of the land affected by the decision.

caveats: www.albemarle.org refuses automated readers, so every County page cited here is an Internet Archive copy (capture dates in the sources). The County's terms bar reposting its words; each County quote has a paraphrase for display.

The Zoning Ordinance itself (County Code Chapter 18) lives on Municode, which may not be scraped or republished. The district summaries in s2 (LI and HI allow manufacturing by right; commercial districts allow retail and instruction; RA allows home occupations and special uses) are an orientation drawn from the County's pages and general knowledge of the ordinance, not a reading of the current use tables. Confirm the exact use name and district list on Municode or with the Zoning Division before relying on them; the County did not publish a page naming the use category for a glass studio, artisan workshop or maker space.

The Zoning Clearance page says a Certified Engineer's Report may be required; whether a gas-fired hot shop needs one depends on the district's performance standards (Zoning Ordinance § 4.14 on Municode), which were not read.

Fees are from the Community Development fee schedule capture of 20 August 2026 plus the 4% technology surcharge. A revised schedule adopted April 22, 2026 takes effect January 1, 2027 (the short_term_rental_registration file records that clearances rise to $140, special exceptions to $1,125 and BZA appeals to $405 on that date); other 2027 amounts were not read.
The fee for a resubmittal after the first on a special use permit, and the Letter of Zoning Compliance fee, were not legible on the fee page capture.
The 2024 Submittal and Review Schedule linked from the Special Use Permits page was not read; check the current schedule for dates.
Privacy: the County pages name individual planners and zoning administrators; only office lines and role mailboxes are recorded.
